message.content: {"question": "A point particle has a potential energy U(x,y,z)=kx²/2+hy³+mgz where k and h are constants (J/m² and J/m³), m is the particle mass and g is the gravitational acceleration. The motion equations are: a) d²x(t)/dt²=-kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=-3hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=-g b) d²x(t)/dt²=-kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=-3hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=-gz(t) c) d²x(t)/dt²=kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=3hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=g d) d²x(t)/dt²=-kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=-hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=g", "options": {"A": "d²x(t)/dt²=-kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=-3hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=-g", "B": "d²x(t)/dt²=-kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=-3hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=-gz(t)", "C": "d²x(t)/dt²=kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=3hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=g", "D": "d²x(t)/dt²=-kx(t)/m; d²y(t)/dt²=-hy²(t)/m; d²z(t)/dt²=g"}, "correct": "A"}
